title: feat(spec): a stored record-form filter at the rule-array doors converts to the rule array where lossless — D2 page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array (#17321)
body:
Part of #17321
Clause-②: no

A stored record-form `filter` at the converged rule-array doors is now converted to the `ViewFilterRule` array wherever that mapping is lossless — a new ADR-0087 D2 conversion, `page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array` (toMajor 18, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`). A filter carrying `$and` / `$or` / `$not` is left byte-identical and is never flattened. `Part of`, not a closing keyword: ruling item 2's printed TODO list is **not** delivered here. It needs changes outside `packages/spec`, and this dispatch told me to stop at that line and report it (see *Stopped half* below).

## The ruling, item by item

Ruling record 5644018752 (director seat, decision batch #121 item 4, maintainer 「同意」):

| # | Ruled | Here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 「A D2 conversion in the `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array` family covering: flat record `{k: v}` → `[{field, operator: 'equals', value}]`; operator object `{k: {$op: v}}` → the mapped operator; several keys → several AND rules; single-level AST tuples where the seat's mapping is total.」 | **Delivered.** `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, and replayed by id from `step18.conversionIds`. |
| 2 | 「A record carrying `$and` / `$or` / `$not` is passed through unchanged and reported as a structured TODO naming the page/block and the combinator — `os migrate meta --stored` prints the list; …」 | **Pass-through: delivered and pinned. TODO list: stopped** (outside `packages/spec`, see below); plus every filter of an inline-row component (contract review 5853094156). |
| 3 | 「The refusal message at the `filter` door gains the "how to fix" sentence (the separate message-gap card is folded in if it is still open; otherwise cross-referenced).」 | The message-gap card #17320 has state `completed`, so it is cross-referenced here. I measured all 12 doors, and each one already gives the "how to fix" sentence. **One gap was found and fixed.** For a record carrying a combinator, the sentence rendered the combinator as a field (`{ field: '$or', operator: …, value: … }`), which does not fix anything. That case is exactly what this conversion leaves at rest. |
| 4 | 「`Clause-②: no` (no accept-set change; a conversion is added to the ledger).」 | Held **because** the conversion is `retiredFromLoadPath`. `normalizeStackInput` (`defineStack` / `os validate`) never replays it, so an author who writes the record form is still refused at the door. Pinned in §7 of the new test. |

C (flattening) is excluded, as ruled: 「C converts combinators by flattening and silently changes what some pages select — excluded on the fault axis alone.」

## Premises, re-measured on this tree (card measured on `501959b72`)

- **The doors still refuse the record form**: yes. All 12 doors listed below answer `invalid_type` at the key, with the prescription.
- **The stored read path still replays conversions without validating**: yes. `conversions/stored.ts` says 「Never throws, never validates」. `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.convertStoredItem` is the item read path: `getMetaItem` for both draft and active rows calls it, and it replays the full chain, retired entries included.
- **No D2 conversion existed for this shape**: yes. At base `49144fcc`, `conversions/registry.ts` held 103 `toMajor:` lines and not one mention of `dataSource`, `defaultFilters` or a rule-array conversion. The family id appeared only as a semantic entry. At head there are 104.
- **The 「one table」**: the doors fold `operator` through `normalizeFilterOperator` (`VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`). The conversion introduces no new operator table. A record `$op` must be a declared `FILTER_OPERATORS` member, and its name without the `$` is folded through `normalizeFilterOperator` into `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`. An AST infix spelling with no rule word (`=`, `!=`, `>=` …) is lowered through `parseFilterAST`, which is the AST's own single sink, and read back from the `$` operator it produces.
- **Seam (objectui)**: read at the `.objectui-sha` pin `f8a9d0fb0596`. `toFilterNode` / `mergeFilterNodes` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`) already lower all three shapes, including a spec `ViewFilterRule[]`, so a stored row served as the rule array renders — except where a block matches the filter against its OWN inline rows. `object-map`, `object-tree`, `object-calendar` and `object-gantt` hand `schema.filter` unlowered to an in-memory `ValueDataSource` (`ObjectMap.tsx:831-833`, `ObjectTree.tsx:835-837`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx:645-647`, `ObjectGantt.tsx:661,865` via `resolveDataSource.ts:70`), whose `find` reads an object `$filter` in the record dialect but an array one as an AST that refuses a rule object and excludes every row (`ValueDataSource.ts:1100-1101`, `:564`, `:600-603`, `:70-73`). So every filter of a component whose rows are inline (data provider `value`, a data array, `staticData`), the binding included, is left as stored (contract review `5853094156`, rework round 1). The same read **changed the mapping in one place**. `convertFiltersToAST` **skips a record key whose value is `null`**, so today that key constrains nothing, whereas an `equals null` rule would test IS NULL. So a `null` value is declined rather than converted. Combinators are lowered at that pin (`$and` / `$or`) or refused (`$not`), so leaving them as stored keeps what the page does today.

## Which doors 「the family」 covers — measured door by door

Each door below refuses `{ status: 'active' }` with `invalid_type` at the key and the rule-array prescription, including the 「Write one rule per record key」 sentence. The conversion reaches exactly these doors. §6 of the test derives this set from `ComponentPropsMap` and `ElementDataSourceSchema` and holds the conversion's reach equal to it.

| Door | Migration entry named by the refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `dataSource.filter` (any page component, `ElementDataSourceSchema`) | `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array` |
| `object-grid` / `object-metric` / `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` / `object-map` / `object-gantt` / `object-tree` / `object-timeline` `.properties.filter` | `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array` |
| `element:number.properties.filter` | `element-number-filter-rule-array` |
| `element:record_picker.properties.filter` | `element-record-picker-filter-rule-array` |
| `object-grid.properties.defaultFilters` | `object-grid-default-filters-rule-array` |

The `filter` of any other component type is not touched (pinned).

## What converts, and what is left exactly as stored

Converts: a flat record, where each scalar value becomes an `equals` rule; an operator object, where each `$op` becomes the mapped operator and several operators on one field become several rules; several keys, which AND; a single-level AST, meaning one comparison or a flat list of comparisons; and `{}`, which becomes `[]`. Values are carried verbatim. Every produced rule must parse against `ViewFilterRuleSchema`, which is the door's own check, so a converted row re-saves cleanly.

Left byte-identical (identity by reference, no notice):

- `$and` / `$or` / `$not`, or any other top-level `$` key.
- An AST `and` / `or` group, or a flat list that nests one.
- `$null` and `$exists`, whose meaning lives in the value and so is not in the one table.
- `like` / `ilike`.
- A `null` value.
- An array or object comparand in equality position, a field reference, an empty operator object.
- Any rule the door would refuse, such as `in` with a scalar or an empty `icontains`.
- Every filter, the binding's `dataSource.filter` included, of a component whose rows are inline (`properties.data` with provider `value`, a bare `properties.data` array, or a truthy `properties.staticData`). The same filter on an object-bound block converts.

Conversion is all-or-nothing per filter, because converting the mappable keys and dropping the rest would widen an AND list.

**Lossless is measured, not asserted** (§4). For every `FILTER_OPERATORS` member, the mapped rule lowered through `parseFilterAST` equals the source FilterCondition. Only `$null` and `$exists` are declined. For every `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` spelling, the mapped rule lowers exactly as the source comparison did. Only `like` and `ilike` are declined.

## Changed published text

**Refusal at every rule-array `filter` door, for a record carrying a combinator.** For every other value the text is byte-identical to base. I measured this by loading base `49144fcc`'s `filter-rule-array.ts` next to head's and comparing the full issue text (`code|path|message`) for 13 inputs: identical for 11 inputs (flat, `{}`, null value, operator object, more than 3 keys, array value, `$text`, string, number, AST array, `Date`), changed for the 2 combinator inputs. New text for `{ $or: [{ a: 1 }] }` at the binding, read from the built CJS `dist/ui`:

```text
`filter` on this element data source takes the ViewFilterRule ARRAY form `[{ field, operator, value }, ...]`, and this value is the MongoDB-style record form this door took before the one-filter-orthography convergence. `$or` is a combinator, not a field, and the rule array has no spelling for it: its rules only AND, so `$or` and `$not` cannot be written as rules at all, and `$and` only as the separate rules it joins. Nothing rewrites a combinator for you — flattening one changes which rows the filter selects — so decide which rows this filter should select, and write the rules that select exactly those. Legacy operator shorthands (`eq`, `gt`, `notIn`, …) are accepted and normalized on parse. Full conversion table: migration `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array`.
```

For a record that has field keys beside the combinator, the rewrite sentence becomes 「Write one rule per field key — they AND — so its field keys become `[…]`.」 and the combinators are named in the plural: 「`$and` and `$not` are combinators, not fields, …」. The code (`invalid_type`) and path (`filter`) do not change. Both cases are pinned in `filter-rule-array-guidance.test.ts` §1 (code + path + text).

**ADR-0087 semantic entries whose prose this PR made false** (published in the upgrade guide):

- `element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array`, `reason`. 「⚠️ Metadata AT REST is deliberately NOT rewritten, and this disposition adds no D2 conversion … so it has nothing to rewrite for this shape …」 is replaced with a paragraph that names the conversion and what it converts. It also names what it leaves as stored and why. It says in so many words that 「`os migrate meta --stored` does not list these rows yet: a row the conversion leaves as stored reports there as already on protocol.」
- `object-grid-default-filters-rule-array`, `reason`. 「Metadata AT REST is deliberately NOT rewritten and this entry adds no D2 conversion …」 is replaced to match. The two sibling entries (`element-number-…`, `element-record-picker-…`) made no at-rest claim and are unchanged.
- The hand-written `step18.rationale` gains one closing sentence naming the conversion. The generated regions of `migrations/registry.ts` were regenerated with `gen:migration-registry`, not hand-edited.

## Stopped half — ruling item 2's structured TODO list (exact sites)

Measured: the existing D2 machinery does **not** report pass-through rows. Ruled item 2's list needs all four of the following, and three of them are outside `packages/spec`:

1. `packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts` + `apply.ts` + `index.ts`. There is no TODO channel. `ConversionContext` offers only `reportConflict`, and `ApplyConversionsOptions` only `onNotice` and `onConflict`. A TODO sink would be a new notice with a new stable code, next to `OS_METADATA_CONVERTED` / `OS_METADATA_CONVERSION_CONFLICT`.
2. `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`. `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` reds a new `code:` stamp in `apply.ts` until a `foreign-vocabulary` row is added. Its two twins are the `OS_METADATA_CONVERTED` and `OS_METADATA_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` rows. **This is why the spec half was not landed alone**: it would turn a gate red outside this lane.
3. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`. `convertStoredItemDetailed` forwards only `onNotice` to `applyConversionsToStoredItem`. `migrateStoredMetadata` decides with `changed = … notices.length > 0`, so a row that emitted no notice is recorded `canonical` and is never itemised.
4. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-migration.ts`. `StoredMigrationRow` has no TODO field, and `formatStoredMigrationReport` has no TODO section. `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts` `runStored` prints `formatStoredMigrationReport` and emits the whole report as JSON, so it needs no change once the report carries the list.

Until that lands, a combinator row keeps loading unchanged, is counted canonical by `os migrate meta --stored`, and is refused at its door on its next save, now with the corrected prescription. The entry prose and the changeset say exactly this.

## Acceptance notes

- **Settled choices, each on the four axes.**
  - *Several operators on one field* (`{ $gte: 1, $lte: 9 }`) convert to one rule per operator. It is the same AND as several keys, so it is lossless. The alternative, leaving such a filter silent and unconverted, is worse on the fault axis.
  - *`null` values are declined.* Converting them would silently change what the page selects, per the pin read above.
  - *All-or-nothing per filter.* A partial conversion widens the filter.
  - *The family is every door the prescription helper serves.* The helper recognises the same record form, the four entries carry the same table, and the doors that joined later (`object-map` / `-gantt` / `-tree` / `-timeline`) name the same migration.
- `.changeset/19514-…` (pending, another card's) says for `object-grid.defaultFilters` 「Stored metadata … keeps loading and keeps rendering exactly as it does today; what changes is that RE-SAVING it is refused」. After this PR that sentence is still true for what the conversion leaves as stored, but not for the converted forms. This PR's changeset states the new behaviour and ships in the same release. Not edited here (carrier: none).
- `$null` / `$exists` operator objects stay unconverted, because the one-table rule excludes value-dependent operators. They are listed by nothing until the stopped half lands.
- **objectui carrier**: `ValueDataSource` refuses a canonical `ViewFilterRule` array, so a spec-conformant filter on an inline-row map, tree, calendar or gantt already renders nothing today, independent of this PR (measured by probe at the pin, round 1 report on #17321). The seat files it in objectui; the inline-rows decline here can be dropped once it lands.
- The `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence needs no `--to 18`: the CLI's default terminus is the highest major with a step (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:88`, `:393`; pinned by `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-default-range.test.ts`).
